title: Flat preservation and compatibility of the fixed residue tensor square
statement: Use [def-weil-pbc-residue-exchange-comparison-interface], [new-integral-residue-derived-pull-square], [new-integral-residue-tensor-presentation], [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal] and [new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal]. For every scheme map f:X→Y the actual ordinary integral pullback preserves flat objects. Give its derived pullback the already constructed monoidal structure induced by that property and the constructed ordinary monoidal structure. For every integral derived complex M on Y, applying f* to the fixed right-tensor presentation on Y and then the oplax tensor comparison equals the fixed restriction/pullback comparison evaluated at reduction(M), followed by restriction of the inverse canonical scalar pull comparison, and then the fixed tensor presentation on X with B_X identified with f*B_Y. Both tensor presentations and the coefficient-pullback isomorphism are explicit constructions before the statement.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument

proof.text: Construct f*B_Y ≅ B_X using the exact pullback comparison with the degree-zero single functor, ordinary comapUpperStarIso, and the residue ordinary monoidal unit. Compose the canonical right-tensor presentation on X with that coefficient isomorphism to define tX.

Inverse image preserves flat module sheaves: flatness is local and invariant under the coefficient-pullback isomorphism. It preserves colimits, so flat resolutions are sent to K-flat resolutions. Use the constructed derived monoidal API with this flat-preservation property.

On flat resolutions the two routes in the square are balanced tensor associativity and multiply the same scalar factors. The scalar-counit identity for the inverse mate identifies the pull-comparison map with this scalar multiplication map. The explicit tensor presentation uses the extension counit and the balanced tensor isomorphism. Uniqueness of left-derived comparisons descends the equality to all M. No flatness of the residue quotient over the integral coefficients is required.
